fuente.nota: Texto recortado por párrafos; sin cambios en las frases.

parrafos: The European Union (abbreviation: EU) is a union of 27 member countries in Europe on the landmass of Eurasia. It was created by the Maastricht Treaty in 1993. It is a unique political organization; in some ways, it acts like a federation, and in other ways, it acts like a confederation. (Political scientists call the EU a "sui generis" organization, which means the EU is so unique that it is hard to compare it to anything else.)

The EU grew out of the European Economic Community (EEC), which was formed by the Treaty of Rome in 1957. It has created a common economic area with Europe-wide laws, allowing the citizens of EU countries to move and trade in other EU countries almost the same as they do in their own. Nineteen of these countries also share the same type of money: the euro.

The Treaty of Lisbon is the most recent treaty that explains how the Union is run. Every member state signed it, to show that they each agreed with what it says. Most importantly, it says which jobs (’powers’) the Union should do for the members and which jobs they should do themselves. The members decide how the Union should act by voting for or against proposals.

The objective of the European Union is to bring its member states closer together, while also respecting human rights, democracy and rule of law. It does this by helping its members to decide on common rules for many things, like law enforcement, passports, and how to trade fairly with each other.
Most members share a common currency (the euro) and most allow people to travel from one country to another without having to show a passport.

After World War II, most countries in Europe wanted to live peacefully together and help one another's economies. Instead of fighting each other for coal and steel, the first member countries-- (West) Germany, France, Italy, Belgium, Netherlands, and Luxembourg-- created the European Coal and Steel Community in 1952. Its job was to make rules for how to trade coal and steel in a fair way, and to make sure its members were following the rules.

In 1993, with the Treaty of Maastricht, the ECSC joined together with a few other international organizations in Europe to form the European Union. Now it would help its member countries work together in many different ways; not only with trade, but also with money, justice (laws), and foreign affairs.

In 1995, the EU created the Schengen Area, and 22 member countries of the EU opened their borders to each other. This means that people can now travel from one country to the other without a passport or identity card.

In 1999, the EU created its own currency, which is called the euro. Many of its member states got rid of their old currencies, and now use the euro. However, a few countries, like Denmark and Poland, chose to keep their own currency.

Over time, more countries have joined the EU. In 2004, ten new countries became part of the EU: Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Slovakia, and Slovenia. In 2007, two more countries, Bulgaria and Romania, joined the EU. Most recently, Croatia joined the EU in 2013. Then, in 2020, the United Kingdom left the EU. As of 2025, there are 27 member countries.
The EU is now the world's largest single market, with a population of about 450 million people. If the EU were a single country, it would be the world's third largest country.

In 2025 there were United States tariffs against the European Union. In April, the EU informed that from April 15, there would be 25% tariffs on some U.S. goods. The situation is sometimes called a trade war.

A person who is a citizen of the European Union can live and work in any of the 27 member states without needing a work permit or visa. For example, a French person can move to Greece to work there, or just to live there, and he or she does not need permission from an authority in Greece.

Products made in one member country can be sold in any other member country without any special permissions or extra taxes. For this reason, the members agree to rules about product safety - they want to know that a product made in another country will be as safe as it would be if it had been made in their own.

The Council of the European Union is the main decision-making group. The cabinet ministers of the member countries meet (Ministers for Foreign affairs, for Agriculture, for Justice, etc...) and discuss issues that are important to them.

Before the Treaty of Lisbon (written in 2007, implemented in 2008) each member state took a turn at being President of the council for six months. For example, from January 2007 until July 2007, Germany held the presidency. The six months before that, Finland held the presidency. Now the President of the European Union chairs the council summits. The President of the council is the organiser and manager and is voted into office for a duration of two and a half years. He or she does not have the power to make decisions about the European Union like the President of the United States does for that country.

Member countries with a large population (Germany, France, United Kingdom, etc.) have more votes than countries with small populations (Luxembourg, Malta, etc.) but a decision cannot be made if enough countries vote against the decision.

Twice a year, the heads of government (Prime Ministers) and/or the heads of state (Presidents) meet to talk about the main issues and make decisions on different issues. This meeting is different and not as formal. It is known as a European Council.

The European Commission runs the day-to-day running of the EU and writes laws, like a government. Laws written by the commission are discussed and changed by the European Parliament and the Council of the European Union. The commission has one President and 27 Commissioners, selected by the European Council. The Commission President is appointed by the European Council with the approval of the European Parliament. The commission operates like a cabinet government. There is one Commissioner per member state, though Commissioners are bound to represent the interests of the EU as a whole rather than their home state.

The Parliament has a total of 720 members (called Members of the European Parliament, or MEP). They are elected in their countries every five years by the citizens of the European Union member countries. The Parliament can approve, reject or change proposed laws. It can also sack the European Commission. In that case, the entire commission would have to give up their jobs.

In 1951, six countries made the European Coal and Steel Community, a basic version of what the EU is now. These six then went further and in 1957 they made the European Economic Community and the European Coal and Steel Community. The UK and others decided not to join, and then when the UK changed its mind it was stopped from joining by French President Charles de Gaulle. When he was no longer President, the UK and others started to join. Today there are 27 members but the idea that more should join is not seen as a good one by everyone.
Serbia, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Turkey and Iceland are "candidate countries"; they are being considered for membership. Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Kosovo are expected to follow.

However, since there have been many political problems happening in Turkey recently, especially with President Edrogan's arresting of tens of thousands of political rivals since the failed coup attempt on July 15, 2016, it is unlikely that it would be allowed to part of the EU anytime soon because EU members believe that the current Turkish government is not respecting human rights, rule of law, or democracy.
On June 23, 2016, the UK held a referendum on whether it should stay in the EU or leave it. The majority [52% to 48%] favored leaving. Britain leaving the EU is commonly known as Brexit.

The government of the UK invoked "Article 50" of the Treaty of European Union (the Treaty of Lisbon) on 29 March 2017. This began negotiations with fellow members of the EU on the terms of exit. The timetable for these negotiations was two years, which meant that the UK would remain a member of the EU until at least March 2019. This deadline was later extended to October 31st 2019 at the request of the British Government. The United Kingdom left the European Union on the 31 of January 2020 at 23:00 (Greenwich Mean Time). Following that, the transition period expired on December 31, 2020 and ended on January 1, 2021.

China–European Union relations. The EU is China's largest trading partner, and China is the EU's largest trade partner. "European Union... agreed [in 2025] to [... put in place] a three-euro duty on low-value imports into [... EU] from July 2026", according to media; That is supposed "to help [against or] tackle a" trade imbalance].
resumen_es: Presenta la UE: su naturaleza, sus orígenes desde la CECA, las ampliaciones, el mercado único, sus instituciones (Consejo, Comisión, Parlamento), los países candidatos, el Brexit y las relaciones comerciales con EE. UU. y China.

ideas_clave.idea: The EU, set up by the Maastricht Treaty and rooted in the 1957 EEC, is a unique 27-member organisation, halfway between a federation and a confederation, that has built a common economic area.

The Lisbon Treaty divides competences between the Union and its members, whose goal is closer integration based on human rights, democracy and the rule of law, including a shared currency and passport-free travel for most.
Born after the Second World War from the Coal and Steel Community of six countries, European cooperation was widened in 1993 to monetary, judicial and foreign policy matters.
The Schengen Area abolished internal border checks and the euro replaced most national currencies, although some states, such as Denmark and Poland, kept their own.
Successive enlargements, offset by the British departure in 2020, have produced a Union of 27 states that forms the world's largest single market, with some 450 million inhabitants.
In 2025 American tariffs prompted EU countermeasures, a dispute described as a trade war.
EU citizens may live and work in any member state without permits, and goods circulate freely thanks to common safety standards.

National ministers meet in the Council, the main decision-making body, now chaired by a president with a two-and-a-half-year term, while votes are weighted by population and heads of government gather twice a year in the European Council.
The Commission, with one member per country serving the general European interest, manages daily affairs and proposes legislation.
The 720 directly elected MEPs can amend or reject draft laws and even dismiss the whole Commission.
Membership has grown from six founders, despite France initially blocking the UK, and several candidates are waiting, although Turkey's accession looks unlikely because of its human rights record.
After a 2016 referendum won narrowly by the 'Leave' side, the UK triggered Article 50, left the Union in January 2020 and completed the transition at the end of that year.
China and the EU are each other's main trading partners, and the EU has agreed a small duty on low-value imports to tackle the trade imbalance.

resumen_modelo: The text offers an overview of the European Union, a 27-member organisation established by the Maastricht Treaty in 1993 which, according to political scientists, is so unusual that it combines features of a federation and a confederation. Its roots lie in the post-war desire for peace: six countries founded the European Coal and Steel Community in 1952, followed by the European Economic Community in 1957. Today, the Lisbon Treaty determines which competences are exercised by the Union and which remain national, and the overall aim is to bring member states closer together while upholding human rights, democracy and the rule of law. Integration later extended beyond trade to monetary, judicial and foreign affairs, leading to the Schengen Area and the euro, although a few members kept their national currencies. Thanks to successive enlargements, the EU has become the largest single market in the world, with around 450 million people, in which citizens may settle and work anywhere and goods circulate freely under common safety rules. Regarding its institutions, the Council, made up of national ministers, is the main decision-making body, whereas heads of state or government meet in the European Council. The Commission runs daily business and drafts legislation, which is then amended by the Council and the 720 directly elected Members of Parliament, who can also dismiss the Commission. Moreover, the article reviews membership issues: several candidate countries are waiting to join, although Turkey's chances are slim owing to concerns about democracy and human rights, while the United Kingdom, after its 2016 referendum, left the Union in 2020. Finally, the text mentions trade tensions with the United States in 2025 and the close but unbalanced commercial relationship with China.

preguntas.enunciado: Busca en el párrafo 0 una expresión latina que signifique «único en su género».
preguntas.pregunta: Find a Latin expression meaning 'unique, in a class of its own'.
preguntas.cita: Political scientists call the EU a "sui generis" organization
preguntas.explicacion: «Sui generis» indica que la UE es tan singular que es difícil compararla con cualquier otra organización.

preguntas.pregunta: Which organisation did the EU grow out of?
preguntas.cita: The EU grew out of the European Economic Community (EEC), which was formed by the Treaty of Rome in 1957.
preguntas.explicacion: El texto dice que la UE procede de la CEE, creada por el Tratado de Roma. Las otras organizaciones no se mencionan.

preguntas.enunciado: Indica si la afirmación es verdadera (V), falsa (F) o no se dice (ND).
preguntas.pregunta: The Treaty of Lisbon sets out which powers belong to the Union and which remain with the member states.
preguntas.cita: it says which jobs (’powers’) the Union should do for the members and which jobs they should do themselves
preguntas.explicacion: El texto destaca como lo más importante del Tratado de Lisboa el reparto de competencias entre la Unión y los Estados.

preguntas.pregunta: What was the main task of the European Coal and Steel Community?
opciones: To set rules for fair trade in coal and steel
To organise free travel without passports
respuestas: To set rules for fair trade in coal and steel
preguntas.cita: Its job was to make rules for how to trade coal and steel in a fair way
preguntas.explicacion: La CECA regulaba el comercio del carbón y del acero y vigilaba que se cumplieran las reglas. La moneda común y Schengen llegaron mucho después; la defensa no se menciona.

preguntas.enunciado: Indica si la afirmación es verdadera (V), falsa (F) o no se dice (ND).
preguntas.pregunta: When the Schengen Area was created in 1995, all EU member states opened their borders to each other.
preguntas.cita: In 1995, the EU created the Schengen Area, and 22 member countries of the EU opened their borders to each other.
preguntas.explicacion: Según el texto fueron 22 países de la UE, no todos. La afirmación cambia ese detalle.

preguntas.enunciado: Busca en el párrafo 8 una expresión que signifique «se deshicieron de», «abandonaron».
preguntas.pregunta: Find a phrasal expression meaning 'abandoned' or 'eliminated'.
preguntas.cita: Many of its member states got rid of their old currencies, and now use the euro.
preguntas.explicacion: «Get rid of» significa deshacerse de algo; aquí, abandonar las antiguas monedas nacionales.

preguntas.pregunta: Which country was the most recent to join the EU, according to the text?
preguntas.cita: Most recently, Croatia joined the EU in 2013.
preguntas.explicacion: Croacia entró en 2013. Bulgaria y Rumanía lo hicieron en 2007 y Eslovenia en 2004.

preguntas.enunciado: Indica si la afirmación es verdadera (V), falsa (F) o no se dice (ND).
preguntas.pregunta: In 2025 the EU announced 25% tariffs on some American goods.
preguntas.cita: In April, the EU informed that from April 15, there would be 25% tariffs on some U.S. goods.
preguntas.explicacion: El texto recoge que la UE anunció aranceles del 25 % sobre algunos productos estadounidenses a partir del 15 de abril, en respuesta a los aranceles de EE. UU.

preguntas.pregunta: Why do member states agree on common rules about product safety?
respuestas: Because goods made in one member state can be sold in any other without special permission or extra taxes, so each country needs to be sure that imported products are as safe as those made at home.
preguntas.cita: they want to know that a product made in another country will be as safe as it would be if it had been made in their own
preguntas.explicacion: La libre circulación de mercancías exige confianza mutua; las normas comunes de seguridad la garantizan.

preguntas.enunciado: Indica si la afirmación es verdadera (V), falsa (F) o no se dice (ND).
preguntas.pregunta: The President of the Council has decision-making powers similar to those of the US President.
preguntas.cita: He or she does not have the power to make decisions about the European Union like the President of the United States does for that country.
preguntas.explicacion: El texto lo niega expresamente: el presidente del Consejo organiza y dirige, pero no tiene poderes de decisión como los del presidente de EE. UU.

preguntas.pregunta: How are votes distributed in the Council of the European Union?
opciones: Countries with larger populations have more votes
Every country has exactly one vote
Votes depend on each country's contribution to the budget
respuestas: Countries with larger populations have more votes
preguntas.cita: Member countries with a large population (Germany, France, United Kingdom, etc.) have more votes than countries with small populations
preguntas.explicacion: El peso del voto depende de la población. El texto no habla de un voto por país, de los fundadores ni de la contribución presupuestaria.

preguntas.enunciado: Busca en el párrafo 19 un verbo coloquial que signifique «destituir».
preguntas.pregunta: Find an informal verb meaning 'to dismiss'.
preguntas.cita: It can also sack the European Commission.
preguntas.explicacion: «Sack» es un verbo coloquial que significa despedir o destituir; en un registro formal se diría «dismiss» o «censure».

preguntas.enunciado: Indica si la afirmación es verdadera (V), falsa (F) o no se dice (ND).
preguntas.pregunta: Each Commissioner is expected to defend the interests of his or her home country.
preguntas.cita: Commissioners are bound to represent the interests of the EU as a whole rather than their home state
preguntas.explicacion: Hay un comisario por Estado, pero debe defender el interés general de la UE, no el de su país.

preguntas.pregunta: Who initially prevented the UK from joining the European communities?
preguntas.cita: when the UK changed its mind it was stopped from joining by French President Charles de Gaulle
preguntas.explicacion: Fue el presidente francés De Gaulle quien vetó la entrada británica; las demás opciones no aparecen en el texto.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is Turkey unlikely to join the EU soon?
respuestas: Because EU members consider that the Turkish government does not respect human rights, the rule of law or democracy, particularly after the mass arrests of political opponents following the failed coup of 2016.
preguntas.cita: EU members believe that the current Turkish government is not respecting human rights, rule of law, or democracy
preguntas.explicacion: La respuesta debe mencionar los valores de la UE que, según los Estados miembros, Turquía no respeta y su contexto (detenciones tras el intento de golpe).

preguntas.enunciado: Indica si la afirmación es verdadera (V), falsa (F) o no se dice (ND).
preguntas.pregunta: The United Kingdom left the EU on 31 October 2019.
preguntas.cita: The United Kingdom left the European Union on the 31 of January 2020 at 23:00 (Greenwich Mean Time).
preguntas.explicacion: El 31 de octubre de 2019 era solo el plazo prorrogado; la salida efectiva fue el 31 de enero de 2020.

qualified majority makes decisions faster
concerns about national sovereignty
passerelle clauses in the Lisbon Treaty
